input.quote: 22.3 A Party may at any time assign, sell or transfer the whole of' its rights and obligations under this Agreement to:
input.rationale: The licence analogue here is the capacity/IRU regime. It sits at (and in part above) our fallback position, so we do not redline it. Affiliate coverage: Subparagraph 12.8 expressly allows a Party to use its WAC to provide services with its Affiliate and the Affiliate of its Parent Company, 12.14 allows Transfer of Allocated Capacity to those Affiliates, and 22.3(c)-(d) permit assignment of the whole to a Subsidiary or Affiliate at any time without Management Committee consent, subject only to timely written notice under 22.6 - i.e. affiliates are covered on written notice. Successor transfer: 22.3(a) permits assignment of the whole to "a successor of that Party" at any time (again notice only, not consent, contrast the 22.2 consent route), and Paragraph 30 binds successors and permitted assigns. Revocability: capacity is held on an ownership basis (12.2) and IRU is an "Indefeasible Right of Use", with reclamation available only for uncured payment default under 23.1-23.2, so the grant is not revocable at the other Parties' discretion - well clear of walk-away. Short of preferred, we note (without flagging) that contractors acting on our behalf are not named in the grant, affiliate use and Transfer carry a Carrier qualification and an Annex 7 cash contribution until the 12.15 relaxation, and 12.23 defers the IRU guidelines and IRU agreement terms to the I&ASC - we should ensure those guidelines do not narrow affiliate or contractor use, noting that "No provisions of the IRU agreement shall override the provisions of this Agreement."

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
mappings.quote: 22.6 A Party exercising its rights under Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 or 22.5 must give notice in writing to all other Parties in a timely manner.

mappings.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
